summary: fractal doctor answers on a busy store: each store check has its own deadline and reports timeout instead of holding the whole report, doctor no longer seals or judges batches to answer, and the claim-signatures count reads its indexes instead of probing every claim

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay changes. Doctor reads what is already sealed and judged.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes or schema-version changes. The claim-signatures count uses the existing claim_verdicts verdict index and the claim_signature_judging pending index while no requeue is pending, and the existing per-claim form while one is.

compatibility.detail: GET /v1/doctor checks can carry the new status "timeout" (with the check's name and elapsed seconds); a timed-out check makes the report's status "fail", so older and newer CLIs both print the partial report and exit non-zero, and this CLI names the checks that timed out. Doctor no longer seals this node's batches or judges their claims first, so right after a write its claim-signatures line can show claims as not yet sealed or unsigned until the daemon's own passes reach them.

downtime.detail: No downtime. Doctor takes no writer.

recovery.detail: Rolling back is safe: the previous doctor seals and judges before reporting, as before.
